# bugs #3727: GCSE uses the value that a global had before a function call in a loop inside an if

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3727/
- Category: [Fixes](../../fix.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17192
- Recommended action: Apply the patch and close.
- Patch: [bugs-3727.patch](../../patches/bugs-3727.patch), commit [`a4f040240`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/a4f040240f6b38199d1fc650f39e7992a240bc36). Applies to r17192 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The program from the ninth comment is in trunk as `support/regression/tests/bug-3727.c`, with its
assertion inside `#if 0`. `SatUpdate` sets the global `n1` to 0, calls `fake ()` in a `for` loop
inside an `if`, and then passes `2*n1` to a function. `fake ()` sets `n1` to 32, and the code that
sdcc generates passes 0. With the assertion enabled, the test fails on mcs51, stm8, and z80.

## Cause

`mergeInExprs` in `src/SDCCdflow.c` computes `inExprs`, the expressions that are available at the
entry of a block. It copies the `outExprs` of the predecessor that dominates the block. For each
other predecessor, it deletes the expressions that `ifKilledInBlock` reports as killed in that
predecessor. For an expression whose result is a global, `ifKilledInBlock` tests whether the
predecessor itself contains a call.

In the test, the loop body contains the call, so `mergeInExprs` deletes `n1 = 0` from the `inExprs`
of the loop header. The block after the loop is dominated by the block of the `if`, and its other
predecessor is the loop header. The loop header contains no call. `n1 = 0` therefore stays in the
`inExprs` of the block after the loop, and `cseBBlock` replaces `n1` by 0 there. Without the `if`,
the loop header dominates the block after the loop, and the error does not occur.

## Fix

When `mergeInExprs` deletes expressions because of a predecessor that does not dominate the block,
it also adds them to the `killedExprs` of the block. In trunk, `mergeInExprs` adds the
`killedExprs` of each predecessor to those of the block, and `ifKilledInBlock` reports the members
of a predecessor's `killedExprs` as killed. With the patch, `n1 = 0` is in the `killedExprs` of the
loop header, and `mergeInExprs` deletes it from the `inExprs` of the block after the loop. The
patch moves the body of `ifKilledInBlock` to a function `killedInBlock`, so that the code it adds
can call the test directly.

## Verification

The patch replaces the `#if 0` block in `bug-3727.c` with `ASSERT (dest == 64)`. Without the change
to `SDCCdflow.c` the assertion fails on mcs51, stm8, and z80.
